title: The balanced tripartitioning tensor P₂ has tensor rank at most 29
statement: Let P_2 = Σ x_A y_B z_C, the sum over all ordered partitions (A, B, C) of {1,...,6} into three 2-sets; it is a 15 × 15 × 15 tensor (Pratt's T_2, arXiv:2311.02774v1, Definition 1.4; the P_2 of Björklund–Kaski–Koana–Nederlof, ICALP 2026). With coordinate i (i = 0..14) of each factor the i-th 2-subset of {1,...,6} in increasing order of Σ_{e∈S} 2^(e−1), the three 15 × 29 integer matrices A, B, C in data/P2_rank29.json (SHA-256 3a46395da0783d3b315509261ea69fb4bb511ce2418a05b432e4bd0bfea32351) have all entries in {−1, 0, 1} and satisfy 4·P_2 = Σ_{r=1}^{29} a_r ⊗ b_r ⊗ c_r over ℤ, where a_r, b_r, c_r are their r-th columns. Hence R_F(P_2) ≤ 29 for every field F of characteristic ≠ 2. Also, for every field F and k ≥ 1, R_F(P_k) ≥ C(3k,k) (conciseness), and C(3k,k) > 8^k C(3k,k) C(2k,k)/27^k exactly for 1 ≤ k ≤ 10, so the inequality of Pratt's Corollary 1.12 holds for these k without hypothesis and no upper bound on R(P_k) with k ≤ 10 can contradict it.

sources.title: A stronger connection between the asymptotic rank conjecture and the set cover conjecture
sources.note: Version v1 read in full. Definition 1.4 (the tensor T_k = P_k of this note); Corollary 1.12 (under the set cover conjecture, R(T_k) ≥ 8^k C(3k,k) C(2k,k)/27^k for every k); §1.2, item 4 of the comments after Corollary 1.12 (p. 4): the upper bound R(T_k) ≤ 8^k/2 for any field with char(F) ≠ 2 (32 for k = 2). Cited as background; not used in the proof.
